thread:
sydney: Heads-up — after yesterday's RBAC cleanup in the priv cluster eu-1 we saw a sudden spike in audit logs and a handful of KMS decrypt failures for private deployments. Anyone oncall?
marcus: Yep, got alerts: multiple 403s for kms:Decrypt starting ~02:40 UTC :rotating_light:. Logs: https://internal/logs/ingest/abcd1234 (redacted)
anya: Is this the patch that removed node-scoped bindings (system:node-proxy etc)? I flagged that could break some node-identity patterns.
sydney: Correct — we tightened node-scoped bindings. Failures all map to pods scheduled on nodes that were just rotated by the autoscaler.
ops-lead: Quick hypothesis: autoscaler replaced nodes -> new node identities aren't present in our KMS key policy (we still use a node-ARN allowlist for decrypt). When decrypt is denied pods retry heavily -> audit-log flood.
sec-bot: Suggested triage commands: `kubectl get pods -n priv-tenant -o wide | grep CrashLoop` and `kubectl describe pod <pod>` to find Node and SA. Also `aws kms list-grants --key-id alias/redwood-priv` to see principals.
marcus: Confirmed. Error from pod logs: `AccessDeniedException: Principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:instance-profile/priv-node not authorized to use kms:Decrypt on key/abc`
anya: Also noticed one rotated node had 12s time drift (chronyd stale). If the node's clock skewed, sigv4 requests to KMS can fail intermittently too.
sydney: For immediate mitigation we have two options: rollback the RBAC patch or add a temporary key-policy entry for the recent node ARNs. Rollback will stop new failures immediately.
ops-lead: Canary rollback already started in eu-1; initiating global rollback now. Meanwhile I'll prepare a hotfix to allow the last 3 node ARNs in the key policy so existing decrypts succeed while we plan a durable change.
marcus: Hotfix steps I'm taking: 1) fetch current policy `aws kms get-key-policy --key-id alias/redwood-priv --policy-name default` 2) create `hotfix.json` to add principals 3) `aws kms put-key-policy --key-id alias/redwood-priv --policy file://hotfix.json` 4) restart kubelet on affected nodes.
sec-bot: Marking audit entries with tag `incident:kms-rbac-1712456789`. Increase index retention for these logs to 90d and create a saved query for all `AccessDenied` with resource-type `kms` and namespace `priv-tenant`.
anya: After rollback and the temporary key-policy patch, the decrypt errors stopped streaming in. Durable fix suggestions: replace node-ARN allowlist with an instance-profile or role-based principal (autoscaler instance profile / node bootstrap role) and use OIDC/STS principals rather than node ARNs that change on rotation. Also bake NTP/chrony into AMI to avoid time skew.
sydney: Agreed. Action list: 1) revert RBAC delta (done), 2) change key policy to allow autoscaler/node-role (not instance ARN), 3) add preflight in RBAC rollout that checks KMS key-policy mapping for any node identities impacted, 4) update AMI to ensure time sync.
ops-lead: I'll open a runbook and assign tasks in the incident tracker. Runbook: https://internal/runbooks/kms-ephemeral-node (placeholder).
marcus: I'll send the hotfix PR for the key policy + short postmortem notes (cause, mitigation, follow-ups).
sec-bot: Noted — tagging PD incident IR-8243 and recording participants. Recommend we add an automated check that compares upcoming node IDs from autoscaler lifecycle hooks against key policy entries during canary rollouts.
anya: Also propose a small e2e test that rotates a node in a staging private cluster and validates KMS decrypt for a test secret before RBAC changes go to prod.
sydney: Thanks all. Follow-up: schedule a tabletop for RBAC rollouts + KMS interplay. @anya @ops-lead please coordinate owners and timeline.
ops-lead: Will do, creating calendar invites and the incident runbook tasks now.
marcus: Closing loop here — errors gone, audit spike subsided, tracking follow-ups in the PR and the runbook.
sec-bot: Incident log entry saved. If anyone finds any lingering 403s ping this thread. :lock:
